humanities_role_explanation: The benchmark evaluates specialized art-historical competence in Christian iconography, testing whether models can identify specific saints based on religious symbols and visual attributes.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Multimodal evaluation where models process images of historical religious paintings alongside text queries, including class names, detailed iconographic descriptions, and few-shot exemplars.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Single-label image classification of religious paintings representing Christian saints, which relies on the visual recognition of characters and attributes as well as iconographic interpretation mapped to the Iconclass taxonomy.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: The evaluation protocol is specifically scoped to the domain of Christian iconography classification across three datasets.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluated multimodal LLMs including GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Gemini 2.5 Flash.

quantitative_metrics.note: Models are evaluated using classification accuracy and cross-dataset prediction consistency.

published_after_march_2023.note: The preprint was published in September 2025.

summary: This study benchmarks Vision-Language Models and Multimodal Large Language Models on single-label image classification of Christian iconography using three datasets: ArtDL, ICONCLASS, and Wikidata. The evaluation explores three distinct configurations: classification with class labels, classification with rich Iconclass descriptions, and few-shot learning. The results show that general-purpose multimodal LLMs outperform fine-tuned supervised CNN baselines on structured datasets, but face challenges with inconsistency and size sensitivity on Wikidata.
key_findings: Gemini 2.5 Pro achieved the highest overall performance, peaking at 90.45% accuracy on ArtDL and 84.82% on ICONCLASS. On the less curated Wikidata dataset, overall performance dropped, with the contrastive SigLIP-SO400M model reaching the highest accuracy of 66.29%, highlighting its robustness to diverse image sizes. Adding iconographic descriptions generally improved zero-shot accuracy, while few-shot learning (with five examples) rarely yielded performance gains and occasionally degraded accuracy.
facets_explanation: The reference labels are retrieved from existing curated metadata based on Iconclass standards in the ArtDL, ICONCLASS, and Wikidata databases. Identifying specific saints within the paintings requires external knowledge of Christian iconographic traditions and symbols, which are not explicitly described within the image stimulus. The evaluation measures accuracy against a single correct class label per image, and the paper does not address annotator disagreement or alternative readings of the visual content.
